text.p: Genetically modified soybeans developed by Monsanto Co. can be segregated from conventional soybeans and should be labeled, EuroCommerce said Thursday.

EuroCommerce, which represents international retailers and wholesalers in 20 countries, rejected a claim last month by the London-based Grain and Feed Trade Association (GAFTA) that labeling was impractical.
"There is consumer demand in Europe for labeling of genetically modfied foodstuffs and retailers insist that raw materials should be separately identifiable," EuroCommerce said in a statement.
European retailers have called for the segregation of U.S. genetically modified soybeans during harvesting, transport and food production so that products can be labelled accurately.

The European Commission last year approved the import of Monsanto's soybeans, which have been modified to resist its Roundup herbicide, despite opposition from environment and consumer groups on health and safety grounds.
